hypothesis: Combining sample-level contrastive repulsion (Decoupled Contrastive Loss) with feature-level dimension decorrelation (Barlow Twins cross-correlation penalty) prevents both sample representation collapse and dimensional redundancy, enabling richer feature utilization across the 2048 projection channels.
rationale: In previous runs, DCL alone achieved our best accuracy (0.6144 in iter 12) by decoupling positive alignment from negative repulsion in sample space. However, contrastive losses in high-dimensional projection space (d=2048) can suffer from feature redundancy where only a subset of feature dimensions carries semantic signal. Barlow Twins cross-correlation loss explicitly forces off-diagonal feature correlations to zero and on-diagonal correlations to one. By constructing a joint objective (DCL + Barlow Twins feature decorrelation), we optimize both sample-space hyperspherical uniformity and feature-space channel independence simultaneously without adding architectural overhead.
expected_effect: Higher linear evaluation accuracy (> 0.6144) due to maximal channel feature entropy and non-redundant representation capacity in the 1.5x anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone.
change_summary:
1. Updated BarlowTwinsLoss to implement a joint DCL + Barlow Twins Feature Decorrelation loss: computes DCL contrastive loss (tau=0.10) alongside batch-normalized cross-correlation matrix penalty (on-diagonal alignment + lambda_param off-diagonal decorrelation).
2. Maintained the best-performing anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone (1.5x width, 768-dim features), 4096-wide 3-layer projection head, and detail-preserving CIFAR-100 augmentations from iter 12.
